  "success_memory_items": [
    {
      "title": "Write a temporary self-test harness before trusting the implementation",
      "pattern": "After implementing the target module, immediately create a throwaway test script (e.g. selftest.mjs / tmp_selftest.mjs) that imports the real module and asserts expected outputs, then run it with node. Keep the harness separate from the deliverable and delete it before finishing.",
      "why_it_helps": "The hidden grader cannot be inspected, so a local harness is the only feedback loop. It converts the spec into executable checks, surfaces wrong assumptions early, and lets the agent iterate on the real module rather than guessing.",
      "examples": [
        "Wrote selftest.mjs importing { encode, decode } and asserting known ciphertexts, then ran `node selftest.mjs`.",
        "Wrote tmp_selftest.mjs for robot-name asserting name format, uniqueness across 300+ robots, and reset behavior.",
        "Wrote selfcheck.mjs for zebra-puzzle asserting waterDrinker()/zebraOwner() and that exactly one arrangement satisfies all facts."
      ],
      "scope": "Single-file JS exercises where the official test file is hidden.",
      "confidence": 0.95
    },
    {
      "title": "Build an independent reference model for differential testing",
      "pattern": "For algorithmic tasks, implement a second, deliberately different computation of the expected result (brute-force search, exhaustive enumeration, or a naive direct formula) and compare it against the real implementation over many generated inputs.",
      "why_it_helps": "A second independent model catches errors that a hand-written example set misses, especially in modular arithmetic, tie-breaking, and combinatorial edge cases. Agreement across hundreds of cases is much stronger evidence than a few fixed examples.",
      "examples": [
        "gen.mjs brute-forced the modular inverse over a in 1..25 and compared against the real encode/decode for many keys.",
        "verify2.tmp.mjs enumerated all reachable tic-tac-toe boards by legal play and compared states against gamestate().",
        "killer-sudoku selftest included 'brute-force agreement (460 cases)' against a naive combination generator.",
        "ledger _selftest3.mjs ran 1232 differential cases against a preserved copy of the original implementation."
      ],
      "scope": "Tasks with a well-defined mathematical or combinatorial specification.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Preserve the original implementation as a differential oracle when refactoring",
      "pattern": "When the task is to refactor existing working code, copy the original into a temporary reference module first, then assert that the refactored version produces byte-identical output across many inputs before deleting the reference.",
      "why_it_helps": "Refactoring risks silent behavior changes. A preserved oracle turns 'looks equivalent' into a measurable parity check, and the differential run localizes any divergence.",
      "examples": [
        "Copied the original ledger.js to _orig_reference.mjs and ran 'differential cases=1232 diffs=0' before removing it.",
        "Kept the reference only for the duration of testing and deleted it in the final cleanup step."
      ],
      "scope": "Refactoring exercises where a correct-but-ugly implementation is provided.",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "title": "Treat the spec text as the source of truth for exact output formatting",
      "pattern": "Extract literal expected strings, punctuation, casing, spacing, and grouping rules directly from the problem statement and encode them verbatim in the self-test, rather than paraphrasing them.",
      "why_it_helps": "Many failures are formatting mismatches (trailing periods, group spacing, capitalization, blank-line placement) rather than logic errors. Verbatim expectations catch these immediately.",
      "examples": [
        "bottle-song selftest embedded the full song lines verbatim from the instructions, exposing a capitalization bug ('Nine' vs 'nine').",
        "house selftest caught a missing trailing period on 'This is the house that Jack built.'",
        "affine-cipher selftest asserted the 5-letter grouping and space-separated ciphertext format."
      ],
      "scope": "Exercises whose correctness depends on exact textual output.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Enumerate boundary and degenerate cases explicitly in the harness",
      "pattern": "Systematically include zero/empty inputs, single-element inputs, maximum/minimum values, invalid keys, and 'just barely valid' cases in the self-test rather than only the happy path.",
      "why_it_helps": "Hidden graders typically weight edge cases heavily. Explicitly testing them forces the implementation to handle them and reveals off-by-one or guard-clause mistakes.",
      "examples": [
        "triangle selftest covered 0,0,0 and degenerate 1,1,2 / 1,2,3 to pin down the '>=' inequality semantics.",
        "affine-cipher selftest asserted that non-coprime a throws and that digits pass through unencrypted.",
        "phone-number selftest covered area/exchange codes starting with 0 or 1 and wrong-length inputs.",
        "killer-sudoku selftest covered size 0, sum too small, and sum too big."
      ],
      "scope": "All specification-driven exercises.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Diagnose failures with targeted one-off probes before editing the implementation",
      "pattern": "When a self-test fails, run small ad-hoc node -e snippets that print intermediate values (character codes, array contents, counts, computed numbers) to locate the exact cause, then fix the implementation.",
      "why_it_helps": "It separates 'my expectation is wrong' from 'my code is wrong' and avoids blind edits. Several runs used this to discover that the test expectation, not the code, was incorrect.",
      "examples": [
        "Printed character codes of a board string to discover a stray character causing a validation error.",
        "Computed 1000000000/(T*period) directly to confirm the implementation's numeric output was correct and the test expectation was wrong.",
        "Printed per-index characters of a ledger row to locate a column-width mismatch."
      ],
      "scope": "Debugging any failing self-test.",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "title": "Clean up all temporary artifacts and verify the final file state",
      "pattern": "Before finishing, delete every scratch/test/reference file and run a final syntax check plus a directory listing to confirm only the intended deliverable remains.",
      "why_it_helps": "Leftover files can confuse the grader or violate the 'do not create test files' constraint. A final listing plus `node --check` confirms the deliverable is syntactically valid and the workspace is clean.",
